messages:
maria: Quick sync — follow-up from the fused-attention RFC. Need to land a kernel-selection policy that covers fused-QKV, fused-bias/rope, and a dropout-free fastpath without blowing up compatibility.
jonathan: +1. What are the hard constraints we agreed on? perf, stability, and deterministic fallbacks?
priya: Yes. Also quantization compatibility (int8/4) and ensuring KV-cache offsets aren't affected by rope variants.
samir: From runtime POV: we need an orthogonal selector that reasons about: op-shape, model-ops (rope/bias present), quant-mode, and preferred fallback order. Prefer not to bake model transforms into kernels.
luca: Proposal: kernel_policy layers -> stage1 shape match, stage2 feature flags (rope/bias/dropoutless), stage3 perf-hint (latency vs throughput). If stage1 fails, fall back to scalar kernels.
maria: Example config sketch:
```
kernel_policy:
  - name: prefer_fused_qkv
    when: [shape.heads==32, dtype==float16, kv_cache==enabled]
  - name: fused_qkv_with_rope
    when: [has_rope==true, dtype in [float16, int8]]
  - name: dropoutless_fastpath
    when: [inference_mode==true]
  - fallback: generic_attention
```
jonathan: Two questions: 1) how do we detect "has_rope" robustly (models may call it different things)? 2) telemetry for policy effectiveness?
priya: For detection, use model metadata when available otherwise scan the attention op attrs at load-time. Add a short heuristic: presence of cos/sin precomputed tensors or named params (/rope/ or sin/cos) — falling back to conservative false if ambiguous.
samir: Telemetry: emit per-request kernel_choice + latency + tokens. Rollout: start with canary traffic at 1% for fused variants, measure time-to-first-token and p50/p95.
luca: Also add health-check hooks: if a kernel results in OOM or wrong-determinism, automatically blacklist for that model-version and route to next candidate.
maria: Edge-case: models compiled with custom fused kernels (third-party). We must avoid re-ordering their kernels. Suggest a model-signature whitelist that prefers model-bundled kernels.
jonathan: Regarding dropoutless: ensure we don't change RNG state expectations. For deterministic seeds, document that dropoutless path bypasses dropout op entirely in inference-mode only.
priya: Perf regression guard: tie model evals to prompt-set tests. If p99 latency increases or model-output diffs exceed threshold, auto-roll back the kernel policy for that model.
samir: Implementation note: keep the selector pure function with small cache keyed by (model-version, seq-len, batch-size, dtype, kv_enabled, quant-mode). That avoids per-request policy recompute.
luca: Compatibility: quantized kernels may have different fused possibilities. Add explicit compatibility matrix: (kernel_name -> supported_quant_modes).
maria: Action items:
- samir: proto for selector API + cache (ETA: Tue)
- priya: detection heuristics + metadata tags (ETA: Tue)
- jonathan: telemetry schema + dashboards (ETA: Wed)
- luca: failure/blacklist strategy doc + canary plan (ETA: Wed)
- I'll draft rollout RFC addendum with explicit gating and rollback thresholds (ETA: Thu)
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline note: remember to add feature-flag gating and a kill switch in the operator for canary groups.
jonathan: One more: we should add a compatibility test that runs a tiny ensemble of models (Llama-like, MPT-like, LLaMA2) through the selector on CI to catch early mismatches.
maria: Agreed. Let's reconvene after the PRs land. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
